review.summary: I reviewed only the two supplied files: src/lib/live-metric-visit-reconciliation.ts and src/lib/live-metric-coverage-reader.ts. I found no BLOCKER and no path where either file reports positive visit coverage. Across all sources, coverage is always unavailable with reason unknown_history or evidence_gap. On the coverage-reader side, visit audit rows can only add gaps, and an evidence gap from the sources wins. These behaviours match the brief: loss markers poison all later windows (any lossAt < T, on any source kind), the window is [S,T), unprepared registration pages that overlap the window are gaps, and unanswered intents stay pending until the version expires. Page, intent and fact scans are each limited to 10001 rows and fail closed above 10000. The window is copied before any await, and the digest leaves out asOf. I found 3 MINOR defects and 1 NIT: (1) an intent counts as answered by any fact with the same visitor, even when the fact's timing is impossible, so a permanent gap can be hidden outside the window; (2) the transaction-local settings stay in effect for the rest of the caller's shared repeatable-read (RR) transaction; (3) when the source scan is unavailable, the reader returns early and drops known gaps from the audit table; (4) intents on viewer/unknown pages are silently left out of the counts. This review does not certify any omitted helpers, schema, roles, the test harness, deployment, or the whole work package. Still open and out of scope: the public SSR 10000 lifetime-quota exhaustion (known MAJOR); positive proof covering every URL and historical form; writer fences and source epochs; coverage for missing, uninstrumented, cached or pre-epoch URLs; popup and multi-session flows; and actual role deployment. One limitation that is not a defect: asOf comes from clock_timestamp() after the RR snapshot, so writes committed later with timestamps before endAt don't show up in this read. That fits the stated 'not a writer fence' design, and only the expired-vs-pending labels can be off.

findings.area: intent loop: `matched=factsByEvent.get(intent.eventId)?.some(fact=>fact.visitorId===intent.visitorId)` and the missing intent/page timing checks
findings.issue: An intent counts as answered by any fact with the same event and visitor, whatever its timestamps. Timing checks (fact before preparation, fact before page issue, preparation before page issue) only run in the fact loop, and only for facts inside the window. If a fact has impossible timing and falls outside the window, it silently closes the intent.
findings.evidence: The fact loop flags `fact.visitedAt<intent.preparedAt || intent.preparedAt<page.issuedAt || fact.visitedAt<page.issuedAt` only after `if(!inWindow(fact.visitedAt))continue`. The intent loop does no such check: any matching visitor clears the pending gap. The brief says registration facts need the exact page, the prepared visitor and valid timing. Facts are unique per scope/visitor/event, so an invalid fact means a valid acknowledgement can never arrive.
findings.impact: A preparation that is permanently unresolved shows as resolved in every later window. Coverage drops from evidence_gap to unknown_history, and pendingRegistrationIntents is undercounted. There is no false positive, because coverage is never complete, but definite negative evidence is lost from the summary and reason.
findings.recommended_fix: In the intent loop, count a match only if it passes the same checks as a valid registration fact: same visitor, fact.visitedAt >= intent.preparedAt, intent.preparedAt >= page.issuedAt, and fact.visitedAt >= page.issuedAt. If a match exists but fails these checks, increment invalidRegistrationChronology (or a new counter) and set hasGap, whether or not the fact is inside the window.
findings.required_test: Unit tests: (a) intent prepared inside [S,T), fact for the same visitor with visitedAt before preparedAt and before S: expect evidence_gap and a timing counter. (b) intent preparedAt earlier than page.issuedAt with a matched fact outside the window: expect evidence_gap. (c) a valid match outside the window still closes the intent and is not counted inside the window.

findings.issue: Both settings last until the caller's transaction ends, not just for this function. The brief says this is the same RR transaction used for report facts and loadMetricViewingSnapshot. Any later query in it runs with row_security=off, and a stricter timeout the caller set earlier is replaced by 5000 ms.
findings.evidence: set_config with is_local=true is scoped to the transaction. Nothing saves and restores current_setting('statement_timeout') or row_security. readMetricCoverage then runs the audit query in the same tx, and other report reads may follow.
findings.impact: Report queries that run later in the transaction behave differently depending on whether visits coverage was read first. A role subject to row-level security (RLS) now gets 42501 errors instead of filtered results, and a caller's tighter timeout can be loosened. This affects availability and predictability; it does not leak data.
findings.recommended_fix: Save current_setting('statement_timeout') and current_setting('row_security') first, then restore them with set_config(...,true) in a finally block. Use the shorter of the existing and desired timeout. Otherwise, document that the caller must apply these settings itself before its first statement.
findings.required_test: Inside an RR transaction, SET LOCAL statement_timeout='1000', call the reconciler, then check that current_setting('statement_timeout') is '1000' and row_security is back to its previous value. Also check that a later fact query by an RLS role behaves as it did before.

findings.issue: For visits, any unavailable result from the source scan (limit_exceeded, or a window ending after asOf, labelled lease_or_scope_unavailable) returns before the audit query runs. Known gap rows in the audit table are never read, so negative evidence that was already recorded is replaced by a generic unavailable status.
findings.evidence: The early return happens before the LiveMetricCoverageAudit query. The brief says an audit gap or a source gap must block completion, and gaps must always survive. A window that extends past asOf also gets the reason lease_or_scope_unavailable even though the lease is valid.
findings.impact: Large versions (more than 10000 rows) and in-progress windows can no longer report known visit gaps from the audit table. Callers get a misleading reason and can't tell a lease or scope failure from a size limit or a window that hasn't closed yet.
findings.recommended_fix: Run the audit query whether or not the sources are available. If the sources are unavailable but audit gaps exist, return the gap evidence, with the source status attached as a non-positive sourceReconciliation. Use a separate reason, such as window_not_closed, when endAt > asOf.
findings.required_test: Visits window with an audit gap row and more than 10000 pages: the result keeps the gap and is never complete. Window ending after the DB clock: the reason is window_not_closed, not lease_or_scope_unavailable.

findings.issue: Intents whose page is viewer or unknown are skipped without being counted, unlike orphan intents and orphan facts, which get their own counters.
findings.evidence: The summary has orphanIntents but no counter for intents on non-registration pages.
findings.impact: The summary is less useful for checking source data. This does not affect coverage.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a nonRegistrationIntents counter, or say in a comment why these intents are expected and safe to ignore.
findings.required_test: Unit test: an intent on a viewer page appears in the new counter and does not change the coverage reason.
